title: Normalized base change of a flat finite type scheme over a Nagata Dedekind ring becomes smooth over the generic points of all fibres after a finite extension

standard_prerequisites.use: Base change compatibility of the smooth locus (Morphisms, set-points-where-fibres-smooth), the finite-extension geometric-reducedness lemmas (Varieties, finite-extension-geometrically-reduced, generic-points-geometrically-reduced, geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open), the extension-of-DVRs formally smooth criterion (More on Algebra, extension-dvrs-formally-smooth), and separability-implies-smoothness (Algebra, separable-smooth); cited inputs with both main paragraphs written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Choose a finite extension L/K over which the reduction of the generic fibre becomes geometrically reduced.
Transfer geometric reducedness to the normalized base change via birationality and get a dense smooth open.
Reduce to the case of dense smooth generic fibre and treat the closed fibres point by point.
Use the solution property of L/K at each DVR to obtain formal smoothness, separable residue extensions, and smoothness of the fibre at the generic points.

proof_roadmap.step: Finite extension kills non-geometric-reducedness of the generic fibre.
Normalized base change acquires a dense smooth open over the new base.
At each closed point, adic formal smoothness from the solution property forces the fibre to be smooth at its generic points.

difficulty_reason: Let A be a Nagata Dedekind ring with fraction field K and X flat of finite type over A with B the integral closure of A in the function field algebra; the theorem produces a finite extension L/K such that the normalized base change Y -> Spec(B) is smooth at all generic points of all fibres. The retained proof is a long structured argument: it repeatedly uses that the smooth locus of a flat finitely presented map commutes with base change; it first picks L/K making (X_L)_red geometrically reduced (Varieties, finite-extension-geometrically-reduced), propagates geometric reducedness to Y_L through birationality and generic-point lemmas, obtains a dense smooth open of Y_L -> Spec(L), and reduces to the case where the smooth locus in the generic fibre is dense; the closing paragraph treats a closed point with maximal ideal m of B: a point y outside the good locus maps to one of the finitely many bad points x_i, O_{Y,y} is a local ring of the integral closure of the corresponding A_i in R(X) tensor L, the chosen extension L/K is a solution for A_i -> O_i so B_m -> O_{Y,y} is formally smooth in the adic topology (extension-of-DVRs criterion), whence the fibre local ring is a field with separable residue extension and the fibre is smooth at y. Retained author proof at lines 19291-19355.
